stem:
Nandini looks at the diagram. Straight lines $JK$ and $LM$ cross at $P$. The marked angle $\angle JPL$ is $81^{\circ}$, and $r$ labels the angle vertically opposite $\angle JPL$.

Which claim correctly gives the measure of $r$?

options.text: $r = 99^{\circ}$, treating an adjacent angle on a straight line as if it were the vertically opposite angle.
$r = 81^{\circ}$, because vertically opposite angles at the same intersection are equal.
$r = 81^{\circ}$, because the angles may be called opposite angles that must sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$r = 81^{\circ}$, only because $81$ is already printed near the crossing.

teacher.key_rationale: Vertically opposite angles at a crossing are equal, so r = 81°. A uses the adjacent supplementary angle instead. C misnames the relation as angles that sum to 180°. D relies on the printed number alone.
teacher.figure_note: Rewritten crossing of JK and LM at P with vertically opposite 81° and r.
